text: Cancoillotte starts from metton, a skim-milk curd pressed and then ripened into hard, yellowish grains; melting it at about 90 °C with water and salt turns it into a runny, low-fat spread whose texture depends on how much water is added.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: The curd is shaped into metton loaves.
The metton is stirred at a controlled temperature until it forms hard, yellowish grains.
The grains are melted with water, salt, melting salts and a little butter.

processing.text: The first steps make the metton, the curd the spread is melted from.
